title: How Lost Can It Be: The Bound on Dead Reckoning Between Fixes, Why It Grows Faster Than the Distance, and When the Robot Must Stop and Ask

questions.question: What should a robot carry with its position between fixes?
options: The time of the last fix only
A number for how wrong it can be
The number of wheel turns since the fix
A flag that says dead reckoning is on
questions.explanation: Between fixes the position is a guess that gets worse. Carrying its covariance says how much worse, so the rest of the robot can decide what it may still do.

questions.question: The 95 percent radius after 10 m, and after 100 m, were:
options: 0.22 m and 2.2 m: ten times for ten times the distance
0.22 m and 7.07 m: 31.6 times for ten times the distance
questions.explanation: A heading that wanders turns into position error that grows with the distance, and the heading error itself keeps growing. That gives the power of three halves.

questions.question: 95 percent of 400 noisy runs ended within:
questions.explanation: The bound was 7.07 m and 95 percent of 400 simulated runs were within 5.10 m. The bound is a little loose because a circle has to hold the long axis of an ellipse.

questions.question: A fix of 5 cm brought the radius down to:
options: 7.07 m: a fix does not change the bound
questions.explanation: The fix's own 5 cm combines with what dead reckoning had, and the radius of 95 percent comes to 0.122 m. Then it grows again.

questions.question: Why does doubling the distance between fixes more than double how lost the robot can be?
options: The wheels slip more on long runs
The heading wanders as it goes and the heading error becomes position error with the distance
It does not: the bound is proportional to the distance
questions.explanation: Distance noise alone adds as a random walk, the square root of the distance. The heading's walk makes the bound grow as the distance to the power of three halves.

questions.question: What does needs_fix say?
options: The robot may now be further out than a limit
questions.explanation: A task that needs the robot within a metre, on a route with no fix for 80 m, cannot be done: the bound passes 1 m after 27 m.
